issue.title: Validate management IP addresses
issue.body: A device was created with mgmt_ip "10.0.0.300" and broke the config push job. When mgmt_ip is set, it must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address; reject the device otherwise with a 400. An empty mgmt_ip is still allowed.

requirements.summary: Reject device create and update requests whose non-empty mgmt_ip is not a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address, returning HTTP 400 and persisting nothing, while continuing to allow an empty mgmt_ip.
requirements: When a device create request includes a non-empty mgmt_ip, the service must verify it is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address before persisting the device.
When a device update request includes a non-empty mgmt_ip, the service must verify it is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address before persisting the change.
If mgmt_ip is not a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address, the service must respond with HTTP 400 and must not persist the device or change.
If mgmt_ip is an empty string, the service must accept the request as it does today.
The 400 response must indicate that mgmt_ip is invalid.
acceptance_criteria: A device create request with mgmt_ip "10.0.0.300" is rejected with HTTP 400 and no device is persisted.
A device create request with a valid IPv4 mgmt_ip such as "10.0.0.12" is accepted (not 400).
A device create request with a valid IPv6 mgmt_ip such as "2001:db8::1" is accepted (not 400).
A device create request with mgmt_ip set to an empty string is accepted (not 400) and stored as empty.
A device create request with mgmt_ip set to a non-address string such as "router-1" or "10.0.0" is rejected with HTTP 400.
A device update request that sets mgmt_ip to "10.0.0.300" is rejected with HTTP 400 and the stored value is unchanged.
A device update request that sets mgmt_ip to a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address is accepted (not 400).
The 400 response body for an invalid mgmt_ip identifies mgmt_ip as the offending field.
assumptions: The validation applies to both device creation and device update, since the issue says 'when mgmt_ip is set' without limiting it to creation.
An empty string is treated as 'not set' and is the only permitted non-address value.
Whitespace-only values are treated as invalid because they are not valid IP addresses.
IPv4 and IPv6 validity follows the standard Go net.ParseIP rules; zone identifiers such as fe80::1%eth0 are treated as invalid.
The existing error response format of the API is used for the 400 response; no new error schema is introduced.
Existing devices already stored with invalid mgmt_ip values are not migrated automatically by this change.
out_of_scope: Fixing or cleaning up existing devices with invalid mgmt_ip values already in the database.
Changing the config push job's behavior or retry logic.
Validating other device fields such as hostname or serial number.
Checking whether the management IP is reachable or unique across devices.
Adding CIDR notation or port number support to mgmt_ip.

plan.reason: Small, stdlib-only validation change in the store. No auth, CI or dependency impact. Note: the API has no general update endpoint. PUT /devices/{id}/status cannot change mgmt_ip, so the update criteria are satisfied vacuously. Do not add an update endpoint; that is out of scope. Putting the check in validate() will also cover any future update path.
steps: In store.go validate(): if d.MgmtIP != "" and net.ParseIP(d.MgmtIP) == nil, return fmt.Errorf("%w: mgmt_ip must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address", ErrInvalid). Do not trim whitespace. net.ParseIP rejects zone identifiers.
Check that Create calls validate() before taking the lock or writing, so nothing is persisted on error.
Check in http.go that status() uses errors.Is so wrapped ErrInvalid still maps to 400.
Check that the POST handler writes err.Error() in the body. If it writes a fixed message, change only that call so the wrapped message (including mgmt_ip) is returned. Never echo secrets.
Confirm SetStatus does not touch MgmtIP. Make no change there.
Add table-driven tests in inventory_test.go. Run gofmt, go vet and go test.
test_plan: TestStoreCreateMgmtIP (table): "10.0.0.12" ok; "2001:db8::1" ok; "" ok and stored empty; "10.0.0.300", "10.0.0", "router-1", " ", "fe80::1%eth0" all fail with errors.Is(err, ErrInvalid). After each failure, Get(id) returns ErrNotFound.

TestHTTPCreateMgmtIP (table, httptest): POST /devices with the same cases. Expect 201 for valid and 400 for invalid. For 400, the body contains "mgmt_ip" and a follow-up GET /devices/{id} returns 404.
Run the existing tests to confirm no regressions, including seed data that uses mgmt_ip values.
Run gofmt -l, go vet ./... and go test ./...

findings.issue: Two update acceptance criteria are not addressed. The API has no endpoint that updates mgmt_ip; only PUT /devices/{id}/status exists. SetStatus does not touch mgmt_ip. The diff has no implementation or test for these criteria.
findings.fix: Ask the requirements owner to mark the two update criteria N/A, since no update route exists. If an update path is intended, call validate on it in the store and add table tests: "10.0.0.300" returns 400 with the stored value unchanged, valid IPv4/IPv6 is accepted.

findings.issue: In TestHTTPCreateMgmtIP the res2 error is ignored and res2.Body is never closed. A failed GET would cause a nil-pointer panic, and the open body leaks a connection.
findings.fix: Check the error from http.Get and close res2.Body, e.g. with defer.

findings.issue: The test compares gerr != ErrNotFound with ==. This breaks if the error is ever wrapped, and is inconsistent with the errors.Is check used just above.
